"Dhurandhar The Revenge" TV Premiere Faces Significant CBFC Cuts

The action saga "Dhurandhar The Revenge," released in 2026, is set for its television premiere on Star Gold on Sunday, October 18, at 7:00 pm, following a successful run in cinemas and impressive viewership on OTT platforms. However, its broadcast debut will feature a significantly altered version due to mandates from the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC).

Originally certified 'A' for its theatrical release, the film underwent review by the CBFC for its television airing. The board has reportedly ordered between 45 to 50 cuts to the movie. This extensive editing is standard procedure for films transitioning from an adult rating to a family-friendly broadcast.

As a result of these modifications, the television version of "Dhurandhar The Revenge" will be approximately 10 minutes shorter than its original cut. The edited film will carry a U/A 16+ rating, indicating suitability for viewing by individuals aged 16 and above, under parental guidance.

The substantial changes highlight the stringent censorship requirements for content aired on Indian television, particularly for films that initially received an 'A' certificate. Viewers anticipating the premiere should be aware of the revised content.

What to watch: How the edited version of "Dhurandhar The Revenge" is received by television audiences.

Connected TV Reshaping Indian Storytelling, Say Media Chiefs

Connected TV is profoundly transforming Indian media, impacting not just how audiences watch content but also the very nature of what companies produce. This significant shift was a key discussion point among executives from Prime Video, Sony, JioStar, Zee, and NDTV at the FICCI-Frames conference in Mumbai. Industry leaders noted that the advent of Connected TV is prompting a re-evaluation of content development strategies across the board.

Prime Video, for instance, is now actively developing shows with an eye toward whether audiences will engage with them collectively. This marks a notable evolution from the early days of streaming, which were predominantly characterized by largely solo viewing experiences. Executives emphasized that the move towards considering shared viewership during content creation reflects a deeper understanding of evolving audience habits and the capabilities of modern platforms.

Gaurav Gandhi, Vice President and Head of Prime Video for Asia-Pacific and Australia-New, contributed to these discussions, highlighting the strategic adjustments being made. The collective sentiment at the conference pointed to a future where content is increasingly tailored for diverse viewing environments, including those that foster communal engagement. This adaptation is seen as crucial for remaining relevant in a dynamic media landscape.

The changing dynamics underscore how technology is driving fundamental changes in creative processes and business models within the Indian entertainment sector, pushing for innovative approaches to storytelling.

What to watch: The future of Indian content creation.

He is credited with the lyrics for films such as Rangeela (1995), Bombay (1995), Daud (1997), Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999), Thakshak (1999) and Yuva (2004).
